items.name: Kerala Ash Gourd Mung Olan
steps: Simmer the soaked mung until it begins to soften, then slide in the ash-gourd batons without breaking them.
Grind the grated coconut with a ladle of hot cooking liquid and fold the pale cream into the tender vegetables.
Draw the pot from the heat, season gently, and perfume the surface with torn curry leaves and coconut oil.
items.guidance: This mild, moist Kerala-style olan is especially gentle when served freshly cooked Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Kerala Pumpkin and Pea Olan
steps: Cook the pumpkin cubes with the crushed cumin until their edges are soft but their centers still hold shape.
Add the peas and a smooth coconut paste, then simmer quietly so the vegetables take up the creamy broth.
Turn off the flame before drizzling over the coconut oil and scattering the torn curry leaves.
items.guidance: Sweet pumpkin and coconut make this olan soothing but naturally substantial Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Kerala Cabbage Carrot Thoran
steps: Crackle the mustard in coconut oil, then wake the curry leaves and turmeric in the fragrant pan.
Toss in the shredded cabbage and carrot matchsticks, cover briefly, and let their own steam soften them.
Uncover while the vegetables remain bright, fold through the grated coconut, and season before serving.
items.guidance: A quick, lightly steamed thoran keeps the vegetables lively and the coconut modest Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Kerala Beet Coconut Thoran
steps: Bloom the mustard and cumin in coconut oil, then add the slit chili and curry leaves for a brief sizzle.
Stir the tiny beet pieces through the tempering, splash in a little hot water, and cover until just tender.
Let any remaining moisture evaporate before turning the grated coconut and salt through the ruby vegetables.
items.guidance: Finely cut beet cooks evenly in this earthy, gently sweet thoran Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Kerala Green Bean Thoran

ingredients.name: Green beans, sliced into small rounds

steps: Toast the split black gram in warm coconut oil until golden, then let the mustard pop around it.
Add the bean rounds with turmeric and a small splash of hot water; cover only until the green color deepens.
Finish uncovered with the coconut and torn curry leaves, stirring until the thoran is moist rather than wet.
items.guidance: Beans and a crisp lentil tempering give this thoran a light, satisfying texture Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Kerala Root Vegetable Avial

ingredients.name: Green plantain, peeled and cut long
Yam, peeled and cut into sticks

steps: Layer the firm yam and plantain beneath the quicker-cooking carrot and beans, then steam them with enough hot water to stay succulent.
Crush the cumin with the grated coconut, loosen the paste with cooking liquid, and ease it among the tender batons.
Lower the heat before folding in the whisked yogurt; warm without boiling, season, and finish with curry leaves and coconut oil.
items.guidance: This substantial avial balances firm roots with a gently tangy coconut coating Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: omit the chili and use mildly sour yogurt. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Kerala Eggplant Theeyal
steps: Brown the coconut slowly with coriander and fenugreek until nutty, then grind the cooled mixture with a little hot water.
Sear the eggplant wedges in part of the oil, pour in the diluted tamarind, and simmer until the flesh yields.
Stir in the roasted paste, reduce to a glossy gravy, and crown it with mustard and curry leaves crackled in the remaining oil.
items.guidance: Roasted coconut and tamarind make theeyal deep and warming rather than light Vata: serve a small portion beside soft rice and add a spoon of ghee. Pitta: reduce the tamarind and omit extra chilies. Kapha: keep the coconut portion modest and emphasize black pepper.

items.name: Kerala Pumpkin Mung Erissery

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Cook the mung until nearly creamy, then add the pumpkin chunks and turmeric so they soften without disappearing.
Blend most of the coconut with cumin and hot broth, and stir this paste into the pot until the lentils coat the pumpkin.
Toast the reserved coconut in coconut oil with mustard and curry leaves, then spoon the bronze tempering over the erissery.
items.guidance: Soft mung and pumpkin give this erissery a nourishing, naturally sweet body Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Kerala Green Plantain Erissery
steps: Boil the soaked mung until tender, add the plantain cubes, and continue cooking until a spoon enters them easily.
Work the cumin and most of the coconut into a paste, then stir it through the thick lentil base without crushing every cube.
Fry the remaining coconut with mustard, pepper, and curry leaves, and spread this crisp tempering across the finished dish.
items.guidance: Plantain makes this erissery grounding, while pepper prevents the finish from feeling dull Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Kerala Chayote Coconut Stew

ingredients.name: Chayote, peeled and cut into cubes
Fresh ginger, cut into thin slivers

steps: Simmer the chayote with ginger slivers until the cubes become translucent at their edges.
Add the peas, then press a smooth coconut paste through the broth and cook just long enough to unite the flavors.
Season off the heat and leave the torn curry leaves to soften beneath a final sheen of coconut oil.
items.guidance: Delicate chayote and coconut form a quiet stew suited to warm-weather lunches Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Kerala Spinach Mung Molagootal
steps: Cook the mung with turmeric until soft enough to mash against the side of the pot.
Wilt the chopped spinach into the lentils, then thicken the green mixture with coconut ground together with cumin.
Let mustard and curry leaves sputter in coconut oil, pour the tempering over the molagootal, and rest it covered for two minutes.
items.guidance: Mung softens the mineral character of spinach in this spoonable Kerala preparation Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Kerala Taro Pepper Curry

ingredients.name: Taro root, peeled and cut into rounds

steps: Parboil the taro rounds until their surfaces lose their raw firmness, then drain them without rinsing away the starch.
Heat coconut oil with cumin, turmeric, and cracked pepper before arranging the rounds in a broad pan.
Turn the pieces carefully as they bronze, add the curry leaves near the end, and season once the edges are crisp.

items.name: Kerala Ridge Gourd Coconut Curry

ingredients.name: Ridge gourd, peeled in stripes and sliced

steps: Simmer the soaked chana dal until almost tender, then add the ridge-gourd slices and turmeric.
Grind the grated coconut with cumin and a spoonful of broth, and fold the paste into the vegetables once they are soft.
Temper mustard and curry leaves in coconut oil, stir them through the curry, and let the pot settle before serving.
items.guidance: Watery ridge gourd keeps this coconut-and-lentil curry lighter than it first appears Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Tamil Chayote Chana Kootu
steps: Cook the soaked chana dal with turmeric until tender yet distinct, then add the small chayote cubes.
Grind coconut and cumin to a soft paste and stir it into the pot when the vegetable turns translucent.
Sizzle mustard and curry leaves in coconut oil, fold the tempering through the kootu, and serve it thick rather than soupy.
items.guidance: This Tamil kootu pairs mild chayote with substantial but well-cooked chana dal Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. items.name: Tamil Bottle Gourd Mung Kootu

ingredients.name: Bottle gourd, peeled and cut into cubes

steps: Boil the mung until it yields to gentle pressure, then introduce the bottle-gourd cubes and cook them until glassy.
Stir in coconut ground with cumin and pepper, keeping enough broth for a soft, ladleable consistency.
Warm the ghee with torn curry leaves, pour it over the kootu, and cover briefly to hold the aroma.
items.guidance: Bottle gourd and mung make a notably soft kootu with a mild pepper lift Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Tamil Drumstick Pepper Kuzhambu

ingredients.name: Drumstick pods, cut into finger lengths

steps: Toast coriander and cumin, crush them with the pepper, and set the coarse spice mixture beside the stove.
Sauté the drumstick lengths in sesame oil, pour over the diluted tamarind, and simmer until the inner flesh is tender.
Stir in the crushed spices and turmeric, reduce the kuzhambu until glossy, and finish with torn curry leaves.
items.guidance: Peppery tamarind gravy makes this drumstick kuzhambu penetrating and distinctly warming Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: reduce both pepper and tamarind and pair the dish with plain rice. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Tamil Eggplant Tomato Gothsu
steps: Cook the split mung until soft while the roasted eggplant cools enough to peel and mash.
Collapse the chopped tomatoes in sesame oil with turmeric, then work in the mashed eggplant and cooked lentils.
Temper mustard, asafoetida, and curry leaves separately, fold them through the gothsu, and adjust it to a spoonable texture.
items.guidance: Smoky eggplant gives body to this tangy Tamil gothsu Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use fewer tomatoes and omit any added chili. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Tamil Okra Mor Kuzhambu

ingredients.name: Okra, trimmed and cut into lengths

steps: Sauté the okra in part of the coconut oil until the cut surfaces are dry and lightly colored.
Blend coconut and cumin with a little hot water, add the paste to the pan, and simmer until the pieces are tender.
Lower the flame before stirring in the whisked yogurt; warm gently, then finish with mustard and curry leaves crackled in the remaining oil.
items.guidance: A carefully warmed yogurt gravy softens okra's drying quality Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: choose a modest serving and increase the mustard and ginger.

items.name: Tamil Cabbage Chana Usili
steps: Pulse the soaked chana dal with cumin and the broken chili until crumbly rather than smooth.
Steam the lentil mixture in a shallow layer, cool it briefly, and break it into tender granules with your fingers.
Stir-fry the cabbage with asafoetida and curry leaves, then toss in the lentil crumbs and season once the moisture has cooked away.
items.guidance: Steamed lentil crumbs turn simple cabbage into a protein-rich usili Vata: cook the cabbage thoroughly and add a little extra oil. Pitta: omit the red chili and season with coriander. Kapha: keep the oil light and retain the warming spices.

items.name: Tamil Green Bean Chana Usili

ingredients.name: Green beans, sliced into tiny rounds

steps: Grind the soaked dal coarsely with fennel and chili, leaving enough texture for distinct crumbs.
Steam the coarse paste until firm, let it lose its surface heat, and crumble it without compacting the pieces.
Cook the bean rounds with asafoetida and curry leaves, then fold in the steamed lentils and toss until the pan is dry.

items.name: Tamil Fennel Lemon Rice

ingredients.name: White rice, cooked and cooled slightly

steps: Spread the cooked grains so their steam can escape while you prepare the tempering.
Toast the split black gram in sesame oil, then add mustard, fennel, turmeric, and torn curry leaves in quick succession.
Fold the fragrant oil through the rice, remove the pan from direct heat, and mix in the lemon juice and salt.
items.guidance: Fennel rounds the bright acidity of this Tamil lemon rice Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use less citrus and allow the rice to cool to warm before eating. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Tamil Tamarind Sesame Rice

ingredients.name: White rice, cooked and cooled slightly

steps: Reduce the diluted tamarind with fenugreek until its raw aroma fades and the liquid becomes syrupy.
Pop mustard in sesame oil, add the peanuts and curry leaves, and stir the darkened tamarind reduction into the pan.
Coat the separate rice grains with the sour paste, sprinkle over the ground sesame, and rest the mixture before serving.
items.guidance: Tamarind and sesame make this travel-friendly rice concentrated and sour Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use a smaller amount of tamarind and serve beside a mild vegetable. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Tamil Coconut Cumin Rice

ingredients.name: White rice, cooked and cooled slightly

steps: Fluff the cooked rice onto a wide tray and separate any clumps while it remains warm.
Brown the split gram and cashew pieces in coconut oil, then add cumin and curry leaves until aromatic.
Turn in the grated coconut for less than a minute, fold the tempering through the rice, and season gently.

items.name: Tamil Black Pepper Sesame Rice
steps: Let the tender brown rice stand uncovered until excess steam no longer dampens the grains.
Pound the toasted sesame with cumin and cracked pepper, keeping the seasoning slightly coarse.
Massage the warm ghee and spice powder through the rice, add torn curry leaves, and taste for salt.
items.guidance: A coarse sesame-pepper powder gives brown rice a warming Tamil finish Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: halve the pepper and replace part of it with fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Tamil Spinach Garlic Masiyal
steps: Simmer the split mung until soft, then heap the chopped spinach over it and cover until the leaves collapse.
Mash the greens and lentils together with a wooden spoon, leaving a few leafy streaks for texture.
Brown the sliced garlic and cumin in ghee, add the crushed pepper, and stir this tempering into the masiyal.

items.name: Tamil Bottle Gourd Poricha Kuzhambu
steps: Pressure-cook or simmer the pigeon pea until creamy while the bottle-gourd dice soften in a separate shallow pot.
Combine the two, then stir in coconut ground with cumin and pepper until the gravy becomes cohesive.
Finish with mustard and curry leaves sputtered in coconut oil, and let the kuzhambu stand covered before ladling.
items.guidance: Creamy pigeon pea gives mild bottle gourd enough body for a complete midday dish Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. items.name: Andhra Tomato Toor Pappu
steps: Cook the pigeon pea with turmeric until it can be whisked into a thick, smooth base.
Stew the tomato wedges and slit chili separately until pulpy, then beat them into the cooked dal.
Crackle mustard and curry leaves in ghee, pour the tempering over the pappu, and season after one final simmer.

items.name: Andhra Spinach Masoor Pappu
steps: Simmer the red lentils with turmeric until they lose their shape and become silky.
Fold in the chopped spinach and cook uncovered just until the greens turn tender and the pot thickens again.
Brown the crushed garlic with cumin and broken chili in ghee, then stir the fragrant tempering through the pappu.

items.name: Andhra Cucumber Mung Pappu

ingredients.name: Cucumber, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Cook the split mung until nearly tender, then add the cucumber chunks and turmeric for the final simmer.
Mash only a portion of the dal so the softened cucumber remains visible in the pale base.
Bloom cumin and ground coriander in ghee, add the curry leaves, and fold the tempering through the finished pappu.

items.name: Andhra Purslane Toor Pappu

ingredients.name: Purslane leaves, washed and roughly chopped

steps: Cook the pigeon pea with turmeric until creamy enough to take a vigorous whisking.
Wilt the chopped purslane in a separate pan, add the diluted tamarind, and simmer away its raw sour edge.
Combine greens and dal, then finish with mustard and curry leaves crackled in ghee before adjusting the salt.

items.name: Andhra Eggplant Peanut Kura

items.name: Andhra Ridge Gourd Chana Dal

ingredients.name: Ridge gourd, peeled in stripes and chopped

steps: Simmer the soaked chana dal until its centers are tender while the grains remain separate.
Add the chopped ridge gourd, turmeric, and slit chili, then cook uncovered as the vegetable releases its liquid.
Warm cumin and curry leaves in ghee, stir the tempering into the thickened dal, and season at the table.

items.name: Andhra Okra Sesame Kura
steps: Warm cumin in peanut oil, add the dry okra slices, and spread them so steam can escape.
Turn the pieces only occasionally until their surfaces are no longer sticky, then dust with turmeric and coriander.
Toss through the ground sesame and amchur, season, and remove the pan once the coating smells toasted.

items.name: Andhra Cabbage Chili Fry
steps: Pop the mustard in peanut oil, then stir in the chopped chili, curry leaves, and turmeric for a few breaths.
Add the cabbage ribbons and peas, toss over lively heat, and cover only long enough to soften the thickest pieces.
Uncover and keep the vegetables moving until the pan is dry, then season and serve while their texture remains distinct.
items.guidance: A brisk Andhra-style fry keeps cabbage light and deliberately spicy Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: omit the chili and add crushed fennel instead. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Andhra Pumpkin Tamarind Pulusu

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into large cubes

steps: Fry fenugreek and mustard in sesame oil, then add turmeric and the pumpkin cubes before the spices darken.
Pour in the diluted tamarind and simmer uncovered until the pumpkin is tender but still angular.
Balance the sour broth with grated jaggery, add the curry leaves and salt, and reduce the pulusu until lightly glossy.

items.name: Andhra Lemon Proso Pulihora
steps: Rake the cooked millet across a tray so the tiny grains cool without clumping.

items.name: Andhra Sesame Eggplant Pulusu
steps: Brown the eggplant quarters in sesame oil, turning them gently so the skins stay attached.
Add fenugreek, coriander, and turmeric, then pour in the diluted tamarind and simmer until the flesh is silky.
Shake in the ground sesame, reduce the gravy around the vegetables, and season only after tasting the concentrated broth.

items.name: Andhra Drumstick Peanut Kura

ingredients.name: Drumstick pods, cut into short lengths

steps: Toast the cumin in peanut oil, add the drumstick lengths, and turn them until their green skins brighten.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, coriander, and turmeric, then cover with hot water and simmer until the inner pulp softens.
Thicken the remaining gravy with the coarse peanut meal, season, and rest the kura so the pods absorb the sauce.

items.name: Karnataka Brown Rice Bisi Bele

ingredients.name: Green beans, cut into short pieces

steps: Cook the soaked rice and pigeon pea together until both are soft enough to merge under a spoon.
Simmer the carrot and beans with coriander, cinnamon, and diluted tamarind until the vegetables are tender.
Combine the two pots, loosen the mixture to a flowing consistency, and finish the bisi bele with salt and warm ghee.

items.name: Karnataka Dill Lentil Saaru

Add the chopped tomatoes and cracked pepper, cooking until their sharp raw scent disappears.
Bloom cumin in ghee, stir it into the saaru with the chopped dill, and stop cooking while the herb remains fragrant.

items.name: Karnataka Chayote Majjige Huli

ingredients.name: Chayote, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Cook the chayote chunks with turmeric until tender enough to cut with the edge of a spoon.
Grind the soaked chana dal with coconut and cumin, simmer this paste around the vegetable, and let it lose its raw taste.
Lower the heat before folding in the whisked yogurt, then finish without boiling with mustard and curry leaves tempered in coconut oil.
items.guidance: Chayote keeps this yogurt-based Karnataka huli mild and moist Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: take a smaller portion and make the tempering more pungent.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Karnataka Green Bean Coconut Palya

ingredients.name: Green beans, cut on a fine diagonal

steps: Brown the split black gram in coconut oil and wait for the mustard to pop before adding turmeric and curry leaves.
Toss in the diagonally cut beans with a splash of hot water, then cover until they are tender but still green.
Cook off the remaining moisture, fold in the grated coconut, and season the palya while it is hot.
items.guidance: Fine cutting and brief steaming keep this Karnataka bean palya light Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Karnataka Beet Sesame Palya
steps: Crackle mustard and cumin in coconut oil, then add the torn curry leaves without letting them scorch.
Scatter in the coarse beet shreds, splash the pan with hot water, and cover until the raw crunch softens.
Uncover, toss with the ground sesame, and cook until the palya is moist but no liquid pools beneath it.
items.guidance: Sesame complements the earthy sweetness of beet in this simple palya Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Karnataka Cabbage Pea Palya
steps: Pop the mustard in coconut oil, then add the slit chili and curry leaves for a short aromatic burst.
Tumble in the cabbage and peas, cover for a few minutes, and let the vegetables soften in their own steam.
Remove the lid while some bite remains, stir through the coconut and salt, and serve the palya promptly.
items.guidance: Cabbage and peas make a quick everyday palya with a fresh coconut finish Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Karnataka Methi Brown Rice Bath
steps: Soften the chopped fenugreek leaves in ghee with cumin until their raw bitterness mellows.
Stir in the soaked rice, peas, coriander, and turmeric, coating every grain in the green mixture.
Pour in hot water, cover, and cook gently until the rice is tender; rest the bath before fluffing and seasoning.
items.guidance: Fenugreek leaves bring a pleasant bitterness to this hearty brown-rice bath Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Karnataka Lemon Jowar Chitranna
steps: Separate the cooked sorghum grains on a platter and allow their surface moisture to evaporate.
Toast the split black gram in sesame oil, then add mustard, peanuts, turmeric, and curry leaves.
Fold the hot tempering into the sorghum, take the pan off the flame, and mix in the lemon juice and salt.
items.guidance: Chewy sorghum gives lemon chitranna a deliberately dry, rustic texture Vata: serve it warm with extra ghee and a moist vegetable. Pitta: reduce the lemon and omit chilies. Kapha: keep the oil and peanuts modest.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Karnataka Coconut Sesame Rice Bath
steps: Loosen the tender brown rice with a fork and keep it covered while the flavoring is prepared.
Brown the cashew pieces in ghee, add cumin and curry leaves, and stir in the coconut just until fragrant.
Fold the warm mixture and ground sesame through the rice, season, and rest the bath for five minutes before serving.
items.guidance: Coconut, sesame, and cashew turn brown rice into a rich Karnataka-style bath Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: halve the nuts and coconut and choose a small portion.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Karnataka Pumpkin Peanut Gojju

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into cubes

steps: Sputter mustard and fenugreek in sesame oil, then turn the pumpkin cubes through the aromatic fat.
Add the diluted tamarind and simmer until the pumpkin yields while retaining its shape.
Stir in the coarse peanuts and grated jaggery, reduce the gojju to a clinging sauce, and finish with curry leaves.
items.guidance: Sweet, sour, and nutty notes meet in this substantial pumpkin gojju Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use less tamarind and keep the tempering mild. Kapha: reduce both peanut and jaggery and emphasize fenugreek.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Karnataka Ridge Gourd Toor Tovve

ingredients.name: Ridge gourd, peeled in stripes and diced

steps: Cook the pigeon pea with turmeric until creamy, crushing a few remaining grains against the pot.
Add the diced ridge gourd and slit chili, then simmer until the vegetable becomes soft and the tovve thickens.
Bloom cumin and curry leaves in ghee, stir this tempering through the dal, and season just before serving.
items.guidance: Ridge gourd adds moisture and lightness to this Karnataka pigeon-pea tovve Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Karnataka Spinach Mung Bassaru
steps: Cook the soaked mung until tender, add the spinach, and drain off most of the green cooking broth into a second pot.
Simmer the reserved broth with chopped tomato, cumin, and pepper until it becomes a fragrant, light saaru.
Mash the remaining beans and greens coarsely, season both preparations, and finish the broth with warm ghee before serving them together.
items.guidance: This bassaru yields both a light spinach broth and a hearty mung side Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use fewer tomatoes and soften the pepper with coriander. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
